items.title: Fred Vasseur furious with latest "unprofessional" Ferrari clash: "It's the same speech as Mexico"
items.summary: Ferrari team boss Fred Vasseur says Charles Leclerc's contact with Lewis Hamilton in the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "unacceptable" and showed "lack of respect for the team", with the Formula 1 team set for fresh crisis talks just three weeks after their spat in Mexico.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: With No. 1 driver backing, we could have beaten Kimi Antonelli to F1 title
items.summary: Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton believes he could have beaten Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli in their battle earlier in the season had he been given more support from Ferrari. The Briton was speaking after the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where he had another clash with his team-mate Charles Leclerc, which sent him into a spin.

items.title: Isack Hadjar says freak Las Vegas front wing failure is “ruining my fun” after podium run collapses
items.summary: Isack Hadjar spent the opening half of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix racing wheel-to-wheel with Formula 1’s frontrunners - even pressing Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen for the lead. Halfway through the 50-lap race, a freak mechanical failure reduced the rest of his night to lonely damage limitation.

items.title: Charles Leclerc: Ferrari must find fix to 'unacceptable' feud after Lewis Hamilton clash
items.summary: Charles Leclerc ended the Las Vegas with a 10-second penalty for an avoidable collision with Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton – and a telling-off from team boss Frederic Vasseur ringing in his ears.

items.title: Charles Leclerc “embarrassed for the team” after costly Las Vegas clash with Lewis Hamilton
items.summary: Ferrari left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix with seven points, two 10-second time penalties, and a fresh intra-team mess to untangle. Starting 10th and 11th after a painful double Q2 elimination, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton spent much of Saturday night fighting over the same stretch of road - until their battle boiled over on Lap 38 at the Turns 7–8 chicane.

items.title: “My mistake was to lift” – Why Kimi Antonelli lost power in Las Vegas F1 victory battle
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli has explained the quirky “mistake” that cost him a shot at Formula 1 victory in the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The fastest driver in qualifying, Antonelli was sixth on the grid owing to a five-place drop for an engine change and was the only top-10 starter on mediums rather than softs, which contributed to a further two-position drop on lap one.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli explains mistake that left him “smoked by the two McLarens” in Vegas
items.summary: Kimi Antonelli looked primed to cap a charge from sixth on the grid with a dramatic last-lap victory at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Instead, one split-second pedal adjustment drained his battery dry - handing Max Verstappen breathing room and dropping the Mercedes driver off the podium entirely.

items.title: Fred Vasseur "more than upset" with "unacceptable" Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc Las Vegas clash
items.summary: Ferrari Formula 1 team principal Fred Vasseur said that Charles Leclerc's clash with Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "completely unacceptable", and added he was "more than upset" that the team's message to its drivers seems to have been ignored again. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the team-mates fought over sixth place around the streets of Las Vegas.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton: Las Vegas penalty "really harsh" as podium chance slipped
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton says his 10-second penalty at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was "really harsh" as his chance of a podium slipped from his fingers during a chaotic race. Hamilton started 11th after both Ferraris were knocked out in Q2.

items.title: George Russell: “I don’t regret it” after crashing out of second at Las Vegas GP
items.summary: George Russell could have played it safe and walked away from the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix with a podium. Instead, the Mercedes driver gambled on a late lunge for second - and watched both his shot at victory and his championship cushion slide into the Turn 5 barrier.

items.title: George Russell explains late-race crash in Las Vegas F1 victory bid
items.summary: George Russell has admitted to making “a high-risk move” after crashing with three laps remaining in Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix in an attempt to clinch victory.

items.title: Five quick takeaways from Las Vegas GP
items.summary: Las Vegas gets the pack race it craved In America's artificial entertainment capital, F1 put the most artificial and entertaining spectacle. How fitting. The yo-yo racing from the early days of the 2026 season was back on full display, with the lack of electric energy available on the Strip's mile long straight bring back battery driven overtaking.

items.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: Max Verstappen wins thriller as Ferraris come to blows
items.summary: Max Verstappen won an eventful Las Vegas Grand Prix, holding off both Mercedes as Formula 1’s novel ‘yo-yo’ racing returned – with no Silver Arrow on the eventual podium.

items.title: Oscar Piastri questions "strange" pace deficit to other Mercedes-powered cars in Las Vegas
items.summary: Oscar Piastri stopped short of echoing the verdict of team-mate Lando Norris that McLaren's straightline speed in Las Vegas was "just shocking". But he did acknowledge that the margin of the deficit to rivals was surprising – especially relative to those using the same Mercedes power units.

items.title: Max Verstappen takes Las Vegas pole despite “weird issues” since Brazil
items.summary: Max Verstappen will lead the field to the green light for Saturday night’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, yet the four-time world champion spent Friday evening fighting his own car as much as his rivals.

items.title: Why Mercedes' tow plan for George Russell fell apart in Las Vegas
items.summary: Qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix was decided as much by slipstreams as it was by actual car and driver performance, and this was very clear when looking at Mercedes. Kimi Antonelli went fastest with a 1m33.893s at the chequered flag, but takes a five-place grid penalty for an engine change.

items.title: Isack Hadjar: “We looked stupid” in Las Vegas as I don’t like slipstreaming
items.summary: Isack Hadjar has admitted to underperforming in qualifying for Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix due to not realizing how powerful the tow would be on this high-speed street circuit.

items.title: Kimi Antonelli and George Russell set for Mercedes talks over Las Vegas GP qualifying woes
items.summary: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli will discuss the fallout from Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying “offline” following confusion over team orders and track position. Traffic played a significant role in qualifying on Friday night with drivers reluctant to go first, considering the advantage of a tow is huge around the low-downforce street circuit.

items.title: Max Verstappen shares theory on Ferrari's lack of top speed in F1 2026
items.summary: Although Max Verstappen was not entirely satisfied with his second-fastest time in qualifying for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix – pointing to a mysterious issue with the RB22 – a glance at Ferrari shows that things could have been considerably worse.

items.title: Fernando Alonso: Honda lacks so much power that rivals take extra margin behind us
items.summary: Fernando Alonso says Honda’s power deficit is so dire that other cars are taking extra margin around the Aston Martins at Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. The Nevadan street circuit was expected to expose the Japanese power unit’s deficiencies, with a near-2km full-throttle portion.

items.title: Max Verstappen reveals mysterious Red Bull issue that cannot be fixed in Las Vegas
items.summary: Thanks to Kimi Antonelli's grid penalty, Max Verstappen will start Formula 1's Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole position, but that is not necessarily a reason for the Dutchman to be satisfied.

items.title: Lando Norris frustrated by McLaren's "shocking" top speed at Las Vegas GP qualifying
items.summary: Lando Norris lamented McLaren’s “shocking” straightline speed after missing out on pole at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. The 2025 world champion was fourth fastest on Friday night in Nevada and 0.351s off pacesetter Kimi Antonelli, with Max Verstappen and George Russell also quicker.

items.title: “We lost one second down the straight” – Charles Leclerc upset with Ferrari’s “crazy” Las Vegas deficiency
items.summary: Charles Leclerc is “very disappointed” with Ferrari’s performance at Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix as both cars were eliminated in Q2. Leclerc and team-mate Lewis Hamilton were fourth and eighth in FP3 - the only dry-weather free practice session - but later endured a tougher qualifying.

items.title: Lando Norris brands McLaren “awful in the straight” despite third on Las Vegas GP grid
items.summary: Lando Norris will launch from third on the grid for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix after setting a 1m34.244s in Q3 - just 0.093 seconds shy of inherited polesitter Max Verstappen and 0.020s behind Mercedes’ George Russell. On paper, locking down the second row looks like a tidy recovery for McLaren.

items.title: Lewis Hamilton reveals Ferrari F1 car damage after Las Vegas Q2 exit
items.summary: Lewis Hamilton put Ferrari's Q2 exit in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix down to energy deployment and floor damage, as the seven-time champion felt he'd rallied from difficulties with overall tyre grip.

items.title: Isack Hadjar: Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in Vegas qualifying tow game
items.summary: Isack Hadjar has admitted that Red Bull "looked a bit stupid" in what became a tow battle at the end of Las Vegas Grand Prix qualifying. He says it "doesn't really matter" where he starts on Saturday night. Hadjar set the fifth-fastest time in Q3, 0.699s behind Kimi Antonelli, while team-mate Max Verstappen took pole after the Italian's five-place grid penalty.

items.title: George Russell: Las Vegas qualifying tow was "too difficult to orchestrate"
items.summary: Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell claimed that getting the perfect tow in Las Vegas qualifying was "too difficult to orchestrate" after he missed out on pole position. Russell set the third-fastest time in Q3, 0.331 seconds behind team-mate Kimi Antonelli and 0.073s off Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

items.title: George Russell slams Max Verstappen after Las Vegas clash: ‘He walks around like he’s bigger and better than everyone’
items.summary: George Russell has hit out at Max Verstappen after they collided in Free Practice 3 at Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. Verstappen overtook the Mercedes ahead of Turn 14 in a quest for free air, but Russell moved to get back ahead, with the Dutchman unsuccessfully closing the door.

items.title: George Russell challenges Max Verstappen following Las Vegas practice clash
items.summary: Any hope that George Russell and Max Verstappen had buried the hatchet evaporated at Turn 14 on Friday night. Hours after banging wheels with the Red Bull driver in final practice at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Russell unleashed a blistering post-qualifying critique - just as the pair locked out the front row for Saturday night’s race.

items.title: Charles Leclerc frustrated after qualifying exposes huge Ferrari deficit in Vegas
items.summary: Charles Leclerc has confirmed that Ferrari "lost one second down the straight" during qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix as his frustration builds following a build-up of mistakes from the team and a Q2 exit. Leclerc qualified 11th, just 0.111 seconds off the Q3 cut-off and one place ahead of a struggling Lewis Hamilton. It was Ferrari's first double Q2 exit since Imola last year.
